title: Pump and sand filter: parts, flow path and valve settings
audience: Pool service technicians who operate, inspect or describe a pump and sand filter on a pool
learningOutcomes: Trace the water path through a centrifugal pump plus a sand filter and its multi-position valve
State what each valve setting does and which settings must never be used while the unit is on
Explain why a filter takes out particles but does not disinfect the water
Identify the warning labels and keep them in place, readable and undamaged

instruction.heading: How the parts connect
instruction.body: Picture the reference unit as four linked stages. A centrifugal pump, with an electric motor driving it, starts the flow. Water enters through a lidded lint and hair catcher whose basket catches the larger objects, then leaves the pump through its discharge port. A hose runs that flow to the control valve sitting on top of a fast-flow sand filter. Inside, the sand catches debris on its upper face, the water seeps through the bed, climbs a central tube, and goes out through the valve on its way to the pool again. As debris piles up the gauge reading rises and the return flow falls. That is the signal that a backwash is due, and “Backwash triggers, rinse and chemical cleaning for the sand bed” explains how to carry one out.

instruction.heading: The valve settings and what they do
instruction.body: The six-way valve gives six working settings and one winterising setting. Filter is the normal running setting: flow passes down through the sand and to the pool again. Backwash reverses the flow through the bed and sends it to waste. Rinse follows a backwash and settles the bed before the water goes to waste. Waste bypasses the filter and empties to the waste connection, which suits vacuuming to waste or drawing the level down. Recirculate sends water round the filter without passing it through the sand. The closed setting stops all flow. The manual is emphatic that the pump must never run against a closed valve, because the air-relief path stops working and pressure can build dangerously. A pump run with no flow is also heavily damaged, and the NO FLOW position must never be chosen while the motor is energised.

instruction.heading: What a filter cannot do
instruction.body: A sand filter takes suspended matter above the waterline. It does not disinfect the pool. Disinfection is a separate step, and the chemistry must be kept in balance for the water to stay clear. Chemistry decisions rest with a qualified pool service or the operator. The manufacturer also states a minimum circulation volume per day.

instruction.heading: Pressure and warning labels
instruction.body: The manufacturer warns that the system runs under pressure. If it is put together wrongly, or if air is trapped in the circulation side, parts can separate and cause serious harm. A warning label is attached to the filter body and must stay there. Any safety label that has become unreadable or is missing needs replacing. The manual forbids testing a filter with air or any gas under pressure, since compressed gas stores energy and can cause severe injury if a component fails.

instruction.heading: Why loss of flow matters
instruction.body: A filter that stops running, or that filters poorly, leaves the water cloudy. Cloudy water hides the floor, so a swimmer may dive into or onto something they cannot see, with a risk of serious injury or drowning. Treat any loss of flow or clarity as a same-day report, as “Supervision, behaviour rules and drowning prevention at home pools” explains.

procedure: Identify the pump, the filter, the valve type and each warning label.
Check that every label is present and readable. Record any that are missing or damaged.
Note the valve setting at the beginning of the visit.
Follow the water path from the pool through the strainer, the pump, the valve, the filter and returns.
Confirm the valve is never left closed while the unit is on.
Record the condition of the pump, filter, valve and hoses, and refer any damage.

workedExamples.situation: A visit finds the warning label on the filter faded to the point of being unreadable. The owner says the filter is old and the label does not matter.
workedExamples.reasoning: The label is a safety item and must stay legible. Record the faded label, tell the owner it has to be replaced, and refer the replacement to the manufacturer or a supplier. Do not remove it, and do not accept the view that it is unnecessary.

workedExamples.situation: The valve handle sits between two settings while the unit is on. The owner says it looks fine.
workedExamples.reasoning: Switch the pump switched off before changing anything, as the manual requires. Shift the handle to a defined setting, check that it locks, and restart only after the setting is confirmed. A handle caught between settings may be partly closed, which must never run with the pump on. Record the event and refer the valve if it will not seat.

equipmentAndPpe: Manufacturer manual for the pump and sand filter model
Gloves and eye protection for work near the valve and hoses
Non-slip footwear and a dry mat near wet equipment
Record sheet for valve setting and label check

commonErrors.error: Running the pump with the valve shut
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the valve sits in a working setting before the pump starts. Never select NO FLOW while the unit is on.

commonErrors.error: Removing or ignoring a warning label
commonErrors.prevention: Keep labels in place and readable, and replace any that are missing or damaged.

commonErrors.error: Treating the filter as a disinfectant
commonErrors.prevention: The filter takes out particles. Disinfection is a separate treatment set by the plan.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a handle between settings is safe
commonErrors.prevention: Switch off, turn the valve to a defined position, and confirm it seats.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The system works under pressure. Incorrect assembly, or air in the circulation side, can cause components to separate and cause serious bodily injury.
Keep the warning label on the filter in place. Keep all safety labels kept in good order and replace any that are missing or illegible.
Never test or pressurise a filter with air or gas.
Never operate the pump with the valve shut. The air-relief mechanism stops working and a dangerous pressure situation can develop. Do not select the NO FLOW setting while the unit is on.
Switch the pump switched off before moving the valve setting.
Inadequate filtration causes poor clarity. Poor clarity can lead to diving into or onto objects that cannot be seen, with serious injury or drowning risk.
The minimum circulation requirement and the design of the filtration system are set by local health rules and the operator plan.
This lesson does not grant a licence for pressure equipment or plumbing work.

qualityStandard: The valve setting is recorded at the start and end of each visit.
Every warning label is confirmed present and readable, or its replacement is referred.
The water path is traced, and any damage is recorded and referred.
documentationEvidence: Record of pump, filter and valve model, valve setting and label check
Referral note for missing labels or damaged components
summary: The filter takes out particles. It does not disinfect the water.
Never operate the pump with the valve shut, and switch the pump switched off before any valve change.
Warning labels stay in place, and a filter is never tested with air or gas.

knowledgeChecks.question: A valve handle is caught between two settings while the pump runs. What is the correct response?
options: Take the warning label off so the handle can be seen and keep the pump running
Keep the pump on, then shift the handle while watching the gauge and the gauge is read each minute
Switch the pump off, set the handle to a defined setting, and restart only once it seats
Force the handle to the nearest setting with a tool while the pump is running

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the manufacturer manual say a filter does for the pool water?
options: It disinfects the water so no chemical treatment is needed
It removes all chemical residues from the water
It takes out suspended matter but does not disinfect the pool

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must a filter never be tested with air or gas at pressure?
options: Compressed gas stores energy, so a failure can cause serious injury or damage
Trapped air in the filter helps the water look clearer for the client
Gas tests are needed only to keep the warranty valid and the gauge must read zero
Air changes the gauge reading but is otherwise harmless and it is quick to do
